newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S.-S.Korea war games off after talks with North.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-S.Korea war games off after talks with North.

text.p: South Korea and the United States on Thursday cancelled joint war games after talks with North Korean officials raised hopes of nudging Pyongyang towards peace.
A South Korean defence ministry statement said "Team Spirit" military exercises were called off to ease tensions on the divided Korean peninsula.
U.S. and South Korean officials met North Korean representatives in New York on Wednesday for a briefing on proposed four-way peace talks, which would also include China.

Afterwards, the United States said it was hopeful the isolated Stalinist North would join talks aimed at securing a formal peace treaty between the two Koreas to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
It was the first time that delegations from the rival Koreas had met face-to-face in the presence of American officials since the war.
The once annual war games in South Korea, bitterly denounced by Pyongyang as preparation for an invasion, have not been held since 1993. A decision on whether to resume them is taken each year.

"The decision to cancel Team Spirit is part of efforts by our two governments to build confidence and to create an atmosphere conducive to the reduction of tensions on the peninsula," the defence ministry statement said.
It added the decision would have no impact on the defence readiness of U.S. and South Korean forces.
The United States maintains 37,000 troops in the South to defend against any North Korean attack.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters after the talks "there were no breakthroughs, but the United States is hopeful that today's talks will lead to North Korea joining the formal four-party talks".
The talks were proposed last April by President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
A senior State Department official said North Korea's attendance at the briefing in Manhattan's Hilton Hotel was a good sign.
"I believe the joint briefing itself is modest progress," said the official.
"North Korean diplomats have sat down with South Korean and American diplomats to talk about the possibility of getting to peace talks and that beats all of the alternatives."
The head of the North Korean delegation said the approximately four hours of discussions -- twice delayed by Pyongyang -- took place "in a sincere atmosphere".
The North Korean team now plans to report to Pyongyang on the discussions, but there was no indication when they might reply to the proposal for four-way talks, U.S. officials said.
Actual negotiations may not start until July, according to U.S.officials.

The senior state department official said the United States had proposed that the four parties meet to discuss an agenda for "a peace mechanism and then a peace agreement, no strings attached, everything's on the table".
The venue and level of such talks would be decided later.
South Korean deputy foreign minister Song Young Shik also described Wednesday's meeting in positive terms.
"We consider that this briefing was very significant," Song told reporters.
Tensions on the Korean peninsula have been fanned by a string of North Korean defections, including by Pyongyang's top ideologue who sought asylum last month in Seoul's diplomatic mission in Beijing.
North Korea is on the verge of famine and is desperate for international food aid.
